title: CONFIRMED L2 — Public product path not launched: the landing renders (dev deploy proves the asset), but production serves it at no URL and roots to the operator password wall
expected: An unauthenticated public buyer at '/' sees the marketing landing and can begin the 20-min evaluation.
got: Live on the dev deploy: '/' renders the full Spark landing (hero, demo CTA, 4 compliance pillars + honest non-certification footnote, sourced ROI band, 4 metered tiers) — shot l2-helena-02-root-cold; /landing and /landing/spark deliver the identical gate output (shots 03/04; redirect in app/landing/page.tsx:6-8). The honest prod statement, unchanged from L1 and re-verified in code this pass: the gate is DEV-ONLY (devAuth.ts:28 DEV_GATE = NODE_ENV !== 'production'), so production '/' always mounts the dashboard (app/page.tsx:6-14) and the fail-closed proxy redirects anonymous visitors to the operator password form (proxy.ts:53-82) — whose live render is shot 05 ('KP — Operator sign-in — This workspace is protected'). A public visitor today gets a password box; the page this journey lives on is served nowhere.
evidence: shots/l2-helena-05-talk-to-sales.text.txt ('Operator sign-in. This workspace is protected. Enter the operator password to continue.')
scope_note: Documented deliberate descope ('top-of-funnel is dark on purpose', devAuth.ts:24-27; docs/DESIGN.md 'Public landing: BUILT, NOT LAUNCHED'). L2 adds the proof the asset is launch-quality when served — which sharpens, not softens, the finding: the missing piece is the gate flip + launch checklist, nothing else.
suggested_acceptance: A signed-out production visitor at '/' gets SparkLanding (gate on the real isOperator cookie, not the dev flag); /about, pricing and the demo CTA reachable without any credential.

title: CONFIRMED L2 — No marketing-to-pilot path, live: 'Talk to sales' lands on the operator password form; 'Start free' either password-walls (prod) or drops an anonymous visitor into the seeded workspace (dev); no signup, contact capture, or checkout exists
expected: From pricing or the post-demo peak-intent moment the buyer can start a pilot: sign up, get an isolated tenant, reach checkout — or at minimum leave contact details.
got: Live: clicking 'Talk to sales' on the pricing band renders 'KP — Operator sign-in — This workspace is protected. Enter the operator password to continue.' (shot 05). Clicking 'Start free' on /about on this dev deploy runs signInDev() and lands the anonymous visitor inside the seeded tenant's full workspace (shot 07) — in production the same handler assigns /login (AboutCurve.tsx:91). The sim's post-run CTA never rendered live (the run failed, see gsim-l2-101) but targets /login in code (SimBar.tsx:52). No registration, lead capture, or tenant creation exists anywhere in the live evidence; checkout stays operator-gated (checkout/route.ts:16-17) and workspace creation locked (workspace-lock.ts:24-27).
evidence: shots/l2-helena-07-about-startfree.text.txt (full seeded workspace after one anonymous click, dev)
scope_note: docs/DESIGN.md names this a known launch blocker; the sequencing behind it (tenancy must complete before self-serve tenants) is real — but live, the funnel still ends one click before money, at an operator password with an off-brand 'KP' header.
suggested_acceptance: At least one completable conversion path from pricing: self-serve signup into an isolated tenant with working checkout, OR an honest pilot-request/contact capture — never the operator password box.

title: CONFIRMED L2 — /about (the one prod-served marketing page) carries no demo CTA: its only actions are Sign in and Start free
expected: The keyless guided demo — the product's strongest proof — is linked from every public marketing surface.
got: Live ARIA of /about: the full page exposes exactly these actions — link Home, button 'Sign in', button 'Start free', link 'Back to home', language switch. No demo affordance anywhere (shot 01 aria). The only /api/demo link in the app remains the unlaunched landing's hero (SparkLanding.tsx:278). The silent-refusal half of the L1 finding (gated deploys bounce /api/demo to '/' with zero feedback, demo/route.ts:32-34) was not exercisable live — this deploy is open and the demo minted fine (sim-run.json entry:200) — it stands on code.
evidence: shots/l2-helena-01-about-cold.aria.txt (actions inventory: Sign in / Start free only)
suggested_acceptance: /about carries the demo CTA; a refused /api/demo lands on a surface that says the demo is unavailable and why, instead of a silent redirect.

title: CONFIRMED L2 — the anonymous keyless demo session reads the seeded tenant's entire dataset: 53 named candidates, scores, offers, hires, and the full sealed decision history
expected: A prospect running the guided sim can never read a real tenant's candidate PII — structural isolation, not configuration.
got: Live, mid-demo, in a session minted solely by GET /api/demo (no credentials): the Pipeline tab renders the seeded workspace's full board — 14 positions, 53 active candidates by full name with match scores, '2 offers with candidates — Adam Sedláček, Anna Bartošová', hires, the activity log (shot 21 + sim-run.json pipeline.textHead); the Analytics tab renders the funnel, ROI, and the tamper-evident decision records for the whole tenant (shot 14-b aria). On this open dev deploy that is the expected configuration (DEV_AUTH-gated env; demoSessionAllowed open) — the finding is the live demonstration that demo-'isolation' is an env flag plus marker convention, not a data-layer boundary: the ~28 workspace-blind tables (workspace-lock.ts:1-16) serve everything to the demo session. Corroborating seam: one anonymous 'Start free' click on this deploy class also lands in the same seeded workspace (shot 07, AboutCurve.tsx:91) — the dev gate is client-side localStorage, so any publicly reachable non-production deploy exposes the tenant.
evidence: shots/l2-helena-21-sim-pipeline.png + .aria.txt (POSITIONS 14 / ACTIVE 53, named candidates, offers, hires)
shots/l2-helena-sim-run.json (pipeline.textHead — the same content, captured in-session)
shots/l2-helena-14-sim-phase-4screen-b.aria.txt (sealed decision records + full analytics for the tenant, same anonymous session)
shots/l2-helena-07-about-startfree.text.txt (the one-click dev-gate variant of the same exposure)
scope_note: The prod default is safely fail-closed (demoSessionAllowed() = false on gated deploys) — credited. But the safety is operator discipline, not structure: the moment the demo entry is enabled on a data-holding deploy (exactly the launch configuration EB-H1-01/03 push toward), this exposure goes live. For a bank buyer this is the first question Legal asks, and today's honest answer is the wrong one.
suggested_acceptance: A demo session provably reads an empty/demo-only dataset on every table (tenancy scoped table-by-table), so enabling the public demo cannot expose tenant PII under any env combination.

title: RE-SCOPED L2 (major→minor) — the canned screening draft (fixed confidence 72) never renders to the viewer in the auto-play run; the screening reasoning actually shown is the REAL wave modal
expected: L1 flagged the demo's screening 'reasoning' as a canned template posing as AI output — l2_priority asked what is actually visible live.
got: Live: the visible screening beat is the real decisions engine's wave modal — '9 matched · 0 auto-rejected · 9 advanced' with genuine per-candidate scores (64–75) and tiered rationales plus the fairness line (shot 14-b). The canned draft is created and programmatically consumed within ~1s (SimulationProvider.tsx:494-495; the Decisions badge blips 15→16→15 across shots 14-b/15) — a skeptical buyer watching auto-play never sees the fabricated confidence-72 rationale. The code gap stands (sim/screen-draft/route.ts:17-23 canned draft undisclosed; offer-draft's 'scaled by fit' overstatement never reached this run), and the draft would surface in step-mode or if a viewer raced to the Decisions queue — hence open, not refuted. Impact re-scored to low frequency/reachability for the buyer's auto-play path.
evidence: shots/l2-helena-14-sim-phase-4screen-b.aria.txt (dialog 'Screening · first automated decision wave' — the real reasoning shown)
scope_note: Keyless-by-design per the journey; L1's 'major' assumed the canned rationale was the buyer-visible reasoning — live it is not (in auto-play). The disclosure ask stands wherever the drafts do render.
suggested_acceptance: Sim-generated drafts carry a 'demo stand-in — deterministic, no AI keys' badge (and drop or label the fabricated confidence number) wherever they can render; no rationale string claims a computation the code doesn't do.

title: NEW L2-only — interview-reminders automation is failing and renders its raw SQL error — 'no such column: slot_at' — in the Pipeline automation strip, visible to the anonymous demo session
expected: Automation jobs either work or fail with a human-readable status; a database error string never renders on a product surface (least of all one a prospect sees mid-demo).
got: The Pipeline tab's automation strip shows 'Interview reminders · On · checked today · no such column: slot_at' — the reminders sweep is failing on every check while claiming to be on, and the raw SQLite error is rendered verbatim. Present both BEFORE the sim run (shot 07) and mid-demo in the anonymous session (shot 21 / sim-run.json) — a standing defect of this deploy's DB schema vs the sweep query, not sim-induced. Code: SchedulerControl.tsx renders reminderRuns[0].error verbatim (:474-477); the due-reminders query references slot_at (schedule-store.ts:396-402); the store's own comment documents exactly this legacy-schema seam (schedule-store.ts:99-107) — the guard fixed index creation but this deploy's schedule_invites still lacks the column for the sweep. Net effect: (a) candidate-facing interview reminders are silently not being sent; (b) a dev-grade error erodes trust on the workspace's front page.
evidence: shots/l2-helena-07-about-startfree.text.txt:79-82 ('Interview reminders / On / checked today / no such column: slot_at')
scope_note: Primarily an internal-user surface (Pipeline is Petra's turf) — surfaced under this journey because the buyer's mid-demo walk displays it; L1 missed it because the surface model didn't execute the reminders sweep against the live schema (an L2-only class of finding by nature).
suggested_acceptance: The schedule_invites migrations run against legacy stores on init (or the sweep guards the missing column); the automation strip shows a human-readable failure ('reminders couldn't run — see logs') with the raw error kept in logs; a regression test runs the sweep against a pre-slot_at fixture DB.

title: NEW L2-only — the live ROI meter contradicts the marketing headline inside the same demo session: pricing claims '60–70% less recruiter time on screening' and points at Analytics → ROI, which shows 'Recruiter time saved 5% · ≈2.3 h/hire'
expected: The pricing band's verify-in-product pointer ('Your own measured savings show live in Analytics → ROI') strengthens the 60–70% claim when followed.
got: The demo's Screen phase parks the buyer on Analytics, where the ROI panel reads: 'ROI — what the automation saved: ≈ 9.2 recruiter-hours · ≈ 5 510 CZK; ≈ 2.3 h saved per hire — about 5% of the ~42 h a hire takes by hand' (shot 14-b) — an honestly computed number over the seeded workspace's automation history that sits an order of magnitude below the 60–70% screening-cut headline she read two minutes earlier (shot 02). The meter is a strength (honest, calibrated framing, per-action breakdown); the contradiction is a demo-data artifact — but it is the exact cross-check the marketing invites, failing during the pitch.
evidence: shots/l2-helena-02-root-cold.text.txt:224-236 ('60–70% less recruiter time on screening' + 'Your own measured savings show live in Analytics → ROI')
scope_note: Both numbers are individually honest (benchmark vs live meter on demo seed). The gap is presentation: the demo-visible seed produces a 5% story while the pitch says 60–70%, with nothing bridging them.
suggested_acceptance: The ROI panel (or the demo's analytics beat) contextualizes low measured savings ('demo workspace — savings scale with volume; industry benchmark 60–70%'), or the demo seed is tuned so the measured number is at least directionally consistent with the claim.

title: STRENGTH CONFIRMED L2 — the bank buyer's compliance story renders live, concrete, and uncontradicted on the public surfaces
expected: A public human-in-the-loop / EU AI Act / GDPR Art. 22 story she can hand to Legal.
got: Live on the landing (shot 02): 'Human in the loop — No candidate is advanced, offered or rejected by the machine alone… by design, not by a setting'; 'EU AI Act ready — treated as high-risk AI'; 'GDPR & Article 22 — consent… human review… see or erase… No solely-automated significant decisions'; 'Provable, not promised — tamper-evident, exportable audit trail… calibrated'. /about closes 'AI does the reading at every step. A human signs every decision.' (shot 01). No contradicting fully-automated claim anywhere in the captured copy. Ceiling: this story still does not render inside the demo itself (gsim-l1-005), and the audit-provenance finding gsim-l2-103 now cuts against 'provable, not promised' — the pillars are public and real, and the product must grow into two of them.
ceiling: Public-surface story only: the demo never names it (gsim-l1-005), and the sealed audit's actor misattribution (gsim-l2-103) currently undercuts the 'Provable, not promised' pillar.
